title: Automatic Multi-Organ Segmentation on Abdominal CT With Dense V-Networks

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Automatic Multi-Organ Segmentation on Abdominal CT With Dense V-Networks》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Automatic segmentation of abdominal anatomy on computed tomography (CT) images can support diagnosis, treatment planning, and treatment delivery workflows.

evidence.text: Automatic segmentation of abdominal anatomy on computed tomography (CT) images can support diagnosis, treatment planning, and treatment delivery workflows.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Automatic Multi-Organ Segmentation on Abdominal CT With Dense V-Networks》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-3】We present a registration-free deep-learning-based segmentation algorithm for eight organs that are relevant for navigation in endoscopic pancreatic and biliary procedures, including the pancreas, the gastrointestinal tract (esophagus, stomach, and duodenum) and surrounding organs (liver, spleen, left kidney, and gallbladder).

evidence.text: We present a registration-free deep-learning-based segmentation algorithm for eight organs that are relevant for navigation in endoscopic pancreatic and biliary procedures, including the pancreas, the gastrointestinal tract (esophagus, stomach, and duodenum) and surrounding organs (liver, spleen, left kidney, and gallbladder).

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Automatic Multi-Organ Segmentation on Abdominal CT With Dense V-Networks》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Abstract · abstract-1-2】Segmentation methods using statistical models and multi-atlas label fusion (MALF) require inter-subject image registrations, which are challenging for abdominal images, but alternative methods without registration have not yet achieved higher accuracy for most abdominal organs.

【Abstract · abstract-1-4】We directly compared the segmentation accuracy of the proposed method to the existing deep learning and MALF methods in a cross-validation on a multi-centre data set with 90 subjects.

evidence.text: Segmentation methods using statistical models and multi-atlas label fusion (MALF) require inter-subject image registrations, which are challenging for abdominal images, but alternative methods without registration have not yet achieved higher accuracy for most abdominal organs.
We directly compared the segmentation accuracy of the proposed method to the existing deep learning and MALF methods in a cross-validation on a multi-centre data set with 90 subjects.
